disagreements.topic: 2028E total EPS after the base/enhanced correction ($13.8 to $14.6)
disagreements.positions: agent_1 $13.8 (framework less an ERCOT haircut), agent_3 $14.1, agent_2 $14.2, agent_4 $14.5, agent_5 $14.6. agent_5 says the Q2 deck raised 2027 enhanced gross margin to $2,825-3,025M (from $2,575-2,775M), so 2027 total is about $12.9 and consensus ($13.34) is only ~3% above the framework. agent_3 also cites a ~$250M 2027 enhanced raise.
disagreements.resolution: The raise was to 2026, not 2027. On the Q2 modeling-inputs slide the columns run 2027 then 2026. The 2027 enhanced adjusted gross margin is unchanged at $2,150-2,550M. The 2026 figure rose from $2,575-2,775M to $2,825-3,025M, which matches the 2026 guide raise to $11.50-12.50. The Performance Incentive Adjustment rose too (2026: -$75M to -$125M). So 2027 total EPS is still about $11.9-12.4 (base $7.60-7.70 plus about $4.0-4.6 enhanced, with buybacks from 361M to 357M shares adding ~1%). Consensus of $13.34 sits ~8-10% above that, and 2028E is about $14.2-14.4. agent_5's $14.6 and agent_4's $14.5 (which leans on the higher 2026 guide carrying forward) are $0.2-0.4 high. That puts their P/E legs about $5-8 high.
disagreements.evidence: Q2 2026 slides (8-K Ex.99.2) 'Additional Modeling Inputs' slide 25 vs March 2026 outlook (8-K Ex.99.1) slide 32, column header '2027 2026', sec.gov

disagreements.positions: The yield is now 6.5% (agents 3, 4, 5) or 6.75% (agent_1), with FCF per share of $15.7 (agent_3, NTM at horizon ~$5.5B), $16.6 (agent_5), $17.0 (agent_1) and $17.3 (agent_4). The legs value the stock at $242-266.
disagreements.resolution: Everyone now uses a yield 125-150bp over the 10y (5.24% on 9/28, FRED), which is consistent. Guided FCFbG of $11.5-13.0B for 2028-29 points to about $5.6-6.2B in 2028. On ~347-355M shares that is $16-17.5 per share, so agent_3's $15.7 is at the low end. 6.5-6.75% gives $245-265. This is judgment, not fact, and I leave it at the spread.

disagreements.topic: Will the February 2027 guide land below consensus? (base rate)
disagreements.positions: agent_5 (new): CEG beat its guidance midpoint every year 2022-25, but its one checkable initial guide (2026: $11.00-12.00 vs ~$11.72 consensus) came in below consensus and the stock fell 7%, so it expects a small dip that then recovers. agents 1-4 treat the reset as a bear-case risk.
disagreements.resolution: The initial 2026 range of $11.00-12.00 is confirmed in the March 2026 outlook (slide 22), and the midpoint was raised to $12.00 in August on commercial outperformance and buybacks. The ~$11.72 consensus figure comes from an aggregator and was not verified. The combination of a guide likely below consensus in February and a history of beats is reasonable, and it fits a left-leaning near-term path with little change to 12-month value.
disagreements.evidence: March 2026 outlook slide 22; Q2 2026 slide 11 (initial vs revised guidance); agent_5-cited 2024/2025 guidance 8-Ks

disagreements.positions: agent_4: the $715M purchase of the 609 MW Rhode Island CCGT from Shell (Sep 10) is a small positive. Other agents do not mention it.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed by Constellation's own release: $715M (~$580M net of first-year tax benefits), immediately accretive, returns above the 10% unlevered hurdle, and 'will not impact' executing $5B of buybacks by end-2027. No 8-K was filed (below the materiality threshold). At ~0.6% of market cap it has no material value effect.

one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: Q3 prints have come Nov 4-8 and no date is announced. RBP bids close Oct 21 but results come Dec 2, and the BRA is in December. The Oct 27-28 FOMC arrives with the 10y at 5.24%, up 30bp in two weeks. All five agents now sit within 0.5-0.51 at spot with ~13% monthly sigma, so I keep their mean.
confidence_reason: The one checkable disagreement left (agent_5's 2027 enhanced-margin claim) is a column misread, but correcting it moves only two agents' fair values by about $5 and the mean by about $2. The rest is judgment on multiples and yields. I shade P(>=K) around spot by 0.3-0.5 points only, which is too small and uncertain to replace the mean.
thesis_break_reason: Unchanged from round 1 and at the agents' mean ($195.8; range $192-200): about 13.6x a framework 2028E of about $14.3 and 15% below the 2026 low of $228.63. The June 2027 unlock and a 10y above 5% can plausibly take the stock to $210-220 without breaking the thesis. A trade below $195 would mean the earnings path itself is breaking: a February 2027 guide well below the framework, failure to contract the 147M MWh open nuclear position at a premium, adverse PJM/FERC co-location or cap rules, or a Crane slip.
key_drivers: The earnings path is the management framework, not consensus. Base EPS is guided at 20%+ CAGR 2026-29 and the 2027 enhanced margin is unchanged at $2.15-2.55B, so 2027 total is about $12.0-12.4 against $13.34 consensus and 2028 is about $14.2-14.4.
Rates: the 10y is at 5.24% (4.94% on 9/17) after the Sep 17 hike, which caps the multiple at about 19x forward and the FCF yield at 6.5-6.75%.

Supply: about 38M Calpine-consideration shares remain with former holders, about 11-13M of them free now and about 25M unlocking on 2027-06-30, against ~$2.8B of remaining buyback authority that is still intact after RISEC.
PJM: capacity is locked at the ~$325/MW-day cap through May 2029. RBP results come Dec 2 and the 2029/30 BRA in December 2026, both under the collar.
Upside optionality: 147M MWh of open nuclear output available for premium PPAs, plus the Crane restart in 2027.

fair_value.reason: 2028E total EPS of about $14.3 (base ~$9.45 plus enhanced ~$4.85, interpolated from the guided 2027 and 2029 tools, with ~1% buyback accretion) x 19x = $272, blended 50/50 with 2028 FCFbG of about $5.9B / ~350M shares = $16.9 at a 6.6% yield = $256. That gives about $264, rounded to $265, ex-dividend. It is down from my round-1 $272 because every agent now uses a higher FCF yield, and against a round-2 agent mean of $266 it removes the ~$0.3 of 2028E EPS that agents 4 and 5 carried above the framework.

summary: In round 2 all five forecasters took up the round-1 fact-checks (the base-EPS framework, the 5.24% 10y, the 25M-share unlock in June 2027). Their fair values fell from a mean of $279 to $266 (range $255-275), and P(>=spot) from 0.536 to 0.508. The one new factual dispute goes against the bulls. agent_5's claim that the Q2 deck raised 2027 enhanced margin misreads the 2026 column, so 2027 EPS stays about $12.0-12.4, roughly 8-10% below the $13.34 consensus, and 2028E is about $14.3. I set fair value at $265, about spot, and the thesis break at $195, shading the ladder 0.3-0.5 points around spot. Confidence is low: this is essentially the forecasters' mean.

sizing.reason: The reconciled fair value (~$265) is at spot, and the checked facts lean slightly negative: consensus about 8-10% above the company's 2027 framework, a 10y at 5.24% and rising, and a 25M-share unlock in June 2027. With 47% realized vol, and a February 2027 guide that will likely land below consensus, cap at 6% (down from 8% in round 1) and stage entry around the November and December events. Liquidity is ample.
